image.alt: A Neon Pothos with heart-shaped leaves in glowing lime-yellow, trailing from a white pot

light.label: Medium to bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates low light, but the leaves darken

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; spreads fast, so keep it trimmed

home_use.note: Trails well from a high shelf; the colour is brightest near a window

snap: A fast-growing trailing vine with heart-shaped leaves in a glowing lime-yellow that lights up any room. It is one of the easiest houseplants to keep and forgives a missed watering. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The pothos is native to the Society Islands in the South Pacific and now grows wild across the tropics, where it climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. The Neon is a cultivated form with bright lime-yellow leaves instead of the usual dark green. Indoors the vines trail 2 m or more, or climb a pole or trellis.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, and never leave the pot standing in water. It droops when thirsty and perks up soon after a drink. Yellow, mushy leaves mean too much water. For the brightest colour give it bright to medium indirect light; in dim rooms the leaves turn darker green, and direct sun bleaches and scorches them.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The neon colour glows even in a plain room, and it is among the toughest and fastest-growing houseplants. Cuttings with a node root easily in a glass of water, so one plant can become many. Trim the vine tips to keep it full, and give it a moss pole to climb for larger leaves.
